name: Schafkopf
description: Schafkopf (Bavarian for 'Sheep's Head') is the soul of Bavarian social culture and one of Germany's most important trick-taking games. Played with a 32-card German deck, it is a game of hidden partnerships, high-impact bidding, and mandatory suit-following. It is famous for its tiered trump system where Obers and Unters are permanent trumps, and its 'Rufspiel' (Calling Game) where you choose your partner by calling an Ace you don't possess. It is as much a social ritual as it is a card game.

history.origins: Derived from the ancient 'Schafkopf' group which also gave birth to Skat. The Bavarian variant crystallized in the late 18th century as the definitive pub game of Southern Germany.
timeline: 1890s: Modern hierarchy (Obers/Unters as top trumps) is standardized.
1980s: The 'Bavarian Schafkopf Association' establishes official tournament rules.
Present: Taught in Bavarian schools and remains a daily occurrence in every 'Gasthaus'.
history.cultural: Schafkopf is the 'Third Language' of Bavaria; understanding the cards is essential for local social integration.
history.evolution: The game moved from a point-based betting game to a highly complex tactical simulation involving multiple contract types like 'Wenz' and 'Solo'.

setup.players: Four players sit crosswise at the table. In Rufer (partnership) play, the declarer and the holder of the called Ace form one team against the other two; in Wenz or Solo the declarer plays alone against the other three. The first dealer is usually decided by drawing from the pack; the player with the highest card deals.
setup.dealing: Each player receives 8 cards (dealt in 4-4 batches).

rules.objective: As a team, score at least 61 points (out of 120 card points).
rules.gameplay: Must follow suit. If void, you can play a trump. If a Trump is led, MUST play a trump. Trick is won by the highest rank of suit or highest trump.
keyRules: Must follow suit; if void may play trump. If trump is led, must play trump if possible.
Declarer bids Rufer (call an Ace for partner), Wenz (Unters only as trumps), or Solo (name trump suit).
Obers and Unters are permanent trumps; in Rufer all Hearts are also trumps.
Target 61 of 120 card points (A=11, 10=10, K=4, O=3, U=2).
Called Ace must be played first time its suit is led; may not be smeared when void elsewhere.

strategy.basic: Ace-Calling Wisdom. If you are calling a partner (Rufspiel), only call a suit where you have at least one other card (to ensure the Ace can be 'Released'). If you are the partner holding the called Ace, keep it until your suit is ledâ€”the Ace MUST be played the first time its suit is led. If you have any 10s and Aces of non-trump suits, play them early to secure your points before the trumps come out.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Overs and Unters' Count: There are 8 permanent trumps (4 Obers, 4 Unters). If you hold two Obers, you are strong. If you see the Ober of Acorns (the 'Alte') played, the power structure of the table shifts. Always track how many of these 8 cards have been played. If you are the soloist and all four Obers are gone, you cannot 'Force' the table easily.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Leading: If the declarer calls for the Ace of Acorns, and you are the opponent holding several Acorns, lead that suit immediately! This forces the caller's partner to play the Ace before they are ready, making it easier for you to trump it with a low Herz card. Schafkopf is won by 'Point management'â€”don't let the declarer's team catch your 10s.
tips: The 'Alte' (Ober of Acorns) is the most powerful card; use it to capture 10s, not 7s.
If you have no Obers and no trumps, stay quiet and wait for the 'Sauspiel' (Rufspiel) to protect your team.

variations.name: Rufer (Rufspiel)
variations.description: Partnership game: declarer calls a non-trump Ace (not held); holder is silent partner. Four Obers and four Unters plus all Hearts are trumps (14 trumps).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Rufer uses same engine as base; trump and trick config unchanged.

variations.name: Wenz
variations.description: Solo: declarer plays alone. Only the four Unters are trumps; Obers rank in natural suits between King and Nine.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Wenz changes only trump set; no schema overrides captured yet.

variations.name: Solo
variations.description: Solo: declarer names any suit as trump (plus Obers and Unters). Declarer plays alone against the other three.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Solo changes trump suit only; no engine overrides needed.
